summary: Phelps County, MO: metal lookout tower erected 1953-54 in Mark Twain National Forest; cab refinished 1969-70; standing but in poor shape at a 2023 visit.

facts.design: metal lookout tower with a cab
facts.status_note: Standing at the August 2023 visit, but in poor shape, especially the cab, and the base is fenced.

access.note: Base is inside a chain-link fence topped with barbed wire (2023 visit); no statement on public access or climbing was found

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service is named administrator (NHLR); River Hills Traveler says the Department of Conservation operated it under an agreement

events.note: NHLR gives 1953-1954; the Missouri Conservation Commission annual report records a new tower in fiscal 1953-54
Visit in August 2023: tower and cab standing, cab in poor shape, base fenced
Registered December 31, 2023; nominated by Rick Brown

evidence.quote: The metal lookout tower was erected in 1953-54 and the cab was refinished in 1969-70.

evidence.supports: tower is in Mark Twain National Forest, Phelps County
evidence.quote: Mark Twain National Forest Phelps County, Missouri

evidence.supports: administered by the U.S. Forest Service
August 2023 visit: standing, poor shape, cab worst
evidence.quote: In August 2023, a visit to the tower showed the tower and cab remain standing, though they are in poor shape (especially the cab).

evidence.supports: base has chain-link fence with barbed wire on top
evidence.quote: The base of the lookout tower has a chain link fence around it with barbed wire on top.

evidence.supports: another Pilot Knob lookout existed in Stone County
evidence.quote: There was at least one other Pilot Knob Lookout in Missouri in Stone County.
the Pilot Knob Tower south of Rolla

evidence.supports: tower on Forest Service land; operated by the MDC under an agreement; writer had seen it as an MDC tower
evidence.quote: I had always viewed the Pilot Knob Tower there as an MDC tower, but it seems it is on Forest Service land and was operated by the MDC through an agreement.

evidence.supports: state annual report FY 1953-54: new tower erected at Pilot Knob
evidence.quote: New tower was erected at Pilot Knob in Phelps County.
The Pilot Knob tower cab was refinished.

evidence.supports: the FY 1953-54 report is the Missouri Conservation Commission's
evidence.quote: Missouri Conservation Commission Annual Report FY 1953-54

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR names the U.S. Forest Service as administrator. River Hills Traveler says the land is Forest Service land and the Department of Conservation operated the tower under an agreement. Both can be true; the agreement itself was not found.

sources.title: Breaking down the differences between the Pilot Knob fire towers

notes_for_editor: Only three readable sources. No height was found in them, so none is recorded. The 2023 visit is the newest condition report. The agency question is unresolved: the River Hills column is undated in the text read, and the 1953 land purchase claimed on a geocache page (GC4AMAQ) was not readable, so it is not used. Built date 1953-54 agrees across sources. No corrections to the record. Status note is included because the cab is in poor shape; the tower is otherwise standing.
